patch.objective: Provide crisis intervention and stabilize a client in acute distress
secondaryObjectives: Advocate for needed services, build service networks and plan discharge, aftercare and wraparound follow-up

sources.cite: Roberts' Seven-Stage Crisis Intervention Model, as summarized in an Office of Justice Programs library abstract: (1) biopsychosocial and lethality assessment, (2) rapport, (3) identify the major problems, (4) deal with feelings, (5) explore alternatives, (6) an action plan, (7) follow-up
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on the OJP abstract page (summarizing fetch); the page gives no full citation, and the chapter itself was not read.

sources.cite: NCTSN and National Center for PTSD, Psychological First Aid, 'About PFA': eight core actions: contact and engagement; safety and comfort; stabilization ('to calm and orient emotionally overwhelmed or disoriented survivors'); information gathering on current needs; practical assistance; connection with social supports; information on coping; linkage with collaborative services
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on the NCTSN page (summarizing fetch with short quotes; page metadata dated 2018). The page does not name grounding techniques; the case's breathing and orienting steps are the author's illustration of stabilization.

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (2021 revision): 1.02 self-determination, limited when clients' actions 'pose a serious, foreseeable, and imminent risk to themselves or others'; 1.03(c)-(d); 1.07(c) minimum necessary; 1.07(d) notice before disclosure; 1.07(j) court orders: ask the court to withdraw or limit the order or keep records under seal; 1.14; 1.17(a)-(b)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on socialworkers.org (summarizing fetch with short quotes; the page shows the 2021 code). Amendments were to be voted 2026-11-18; recheck by 2026-12-15.

sources.cite: ASWB Examination Guidebook (August 2026), Clinical and Masters content outlines: I Values and Ethics (Clinical 36%, Masters 35%); II Assessment and Planning (32%, 33%); III Intervention and Practice (32% each); the 2026 blueprints in use from 2026-08-03
sources.note: Relayed from the REQ-288 sessions (read in full 2026-11-14 for REQ-286); not re-read for this case.

brief.situation: You are a licensed social worker at a community mental health agency's walk-in crisis hour. Marisol Vega, 38 (a fictional client), comes in at nine. A fire destroyed her apartment building last night; she and her two children, 7 and 11, got out. The children are at her cousin's. She has a plastic bag of papers and the clothes she slept in. You have an hour.
